messages:
sarah-se: Hey team — POC customer (SDI Health) is connecting via Azure ExpressRoute. They require original client source IPs to show up in their downstream firewall for logging/geo/rate rules. Can Redwood Private be deployed in a way that preserves client src IP end-to-end, or do we have SNAT constraints? Any recommended architectures? cc @mike-netops @alexa-eng

mike-netops: Short answer: it depends on the network path. If traffic traverses an Azure NAT Gateway / Azure Load Balancer outbound, the src IP will be SNATed. Options we can propose:
- Customer-managed egress proxy or NAT device in their VNet or on-prem (preserve IP via X-Forwarded-For / PROXY protocol or avoid SNAT).
- Peer the customer's vNet / route over ExpressRoute directly to the subnets where Redwood Private nodes live — that preserves client IPs if no SNAT is applied in the path.
- PrivateLink-style interface endpoints alone will still depend on upstream SNAT behavior. PrivateLink doesn't magically stop SNAT if an outbound NAT is in front.

alexa-eng: Quick infra detail: our Private deployment attaches into the customer's VNet (like an ENI). If the customer constructs L3 routing (peering/ExpressRoute) to that subnet, packets keep original src IP. The common pitfall: putting Azure NAT Gateway or an outbound LB in front of the flow causes SNAT. So the requirement is: ensure no SNAT between client -> customer edge -> Redwood node.

jordan-sales: Customer also requires a single static egress IP for partner allowlists. If we recommend a customer-managed NAT/proxy, who pays for it and do we offer a managed option? Any pricing notes?

mike-netops: Pricing/ops notes: static egress IP is typically a customer responsibility (cloud provider charges). For Redwood Private we don't add a platform line-item for their NAT, but we can provide a managed egress proxy as an add-on (PS engagement) — that'll be quoted separately. If they want Redwood to front traffic with our IPs, that's a special managed configuration and has support/SLAs attached. I'll follow up with a ballpark PS estimate.

sarah-se: Customer asked for the minimal firewall rules to open from their side. Draft snippet: 
```
# minimal outbound from customer VNet/firewall to Redwood Private
allow tcp 443 -> <redwood-control-plane> (control plane API & heartbeat)
allow tcp 443 -> <redwood-registry> (model pulls / downloads)
allow tcp 443 -> <metrics.ingest> (optional monitoring)
# if you use a proxy, allow proxy IPs/ports instead
```

alexa-eng: Also flag about TLS inspection / SNI: if they terminate TLS in the middle (TLS-inspecting NGFW), routing by SNI may break. Recommend either mTLS to control plane (we support client certs) or place a transparent proxy that preserves SNI/Forwarded headers. If partner integrations require client source IP header, prefer PROXY protocol from the proxy to the FW.

netbot: deploy-bot: created deployment sdipoc-private-1 (id 2750012355) :white_check_mark:

sarah-se: Great, I'll update the security questionnaire with: "source IP preserved with peering/ExpressRoute w/o NAT; otherwise customer must provide NAT/proxy and accept SNAT or forward original IPs via proxy headers." Attaching this thread to the deal doc and looping in sales ENG for the quote. :thumbsup:
